decision.v1_batched_adapter: same existing weights; measured token, EOS, and native-output agreement with rounding-bounded embeddings
decision.v2_optimizer: experimental_not_promoted; heldout reconstruction did not improve consistently and regressed

conclusions: Early selected epochs are not early optimizer termination. V2 trained through epochs330-490; no numerical deadline was exhausted.
Candidate weighted objective continued improving after epoch50-80 selection. The learning-rate scheduler correctly treated such progress separately from saved-state acceptance.

Later generated candidates traded protected modality/privacy/role accuracy for other fields. No subsequent candidate met every per-field gate; many also breached the initial projected-embedding MSE bound.
Primary rejection strings undercount embedding violations because generated-field rejection is checked first; the conjunction table exposes both causes.

Mean-over384-coordinate reconstruction MSE times0.1 is a small continuous loss contribution relative to token cross-entropy. A separate hard MSE gate can reject an objectively better token trajectory; this is a constraint, not evidence the gate should be removed.
The compared training changes are coupled (weighting, generated selection, schedule and batching); these receipts do not identify an isolated causal effect of one parameter.
Preserve inference batching independently on immutable v1 weights; do not promote the v2 optimizer based on syntax validity, lower reconstruction MSE, or faster public inference.
Further objective/source-conditioning work requires a preregistered development comparison followed by new independent test compositions. This completed test must not guide hyperparameter choices.
